final_message:
`int_to_roman(4)` now returns `'IV'`. The function only had the plain symbols (M, D, C, L, X, V, I), so it could never write a subtractive form. I added the pairs 900, 400, 90, 40, 9 and 4 (CM, CD, XC, XL, IX, IV) to the lookup table in `src/roman.py`.

I ran it after the change. `int_to_roman(4)` gives `'IV'` and `int_to_roman(1994)` gives `'MCMXCIV'`. For every number from 1 to 3999, converting to Roman and back with `roman_to_int` returns the original number. The repo has no test file, so I checked with an ad-hoc script and didn't add a test.
